Soap Project Measure 016

Our class checked soap use beside the washbasins. We marked the level in each bottle every afternoon for a week. The bottle near the playground emptied fastest. One pupil said children there must wash their hands more carefully. The caretaker showed us that its pump released more soap with each press. Another bottle had a small leak. We added these details to our notes. The levels told us how much soap had left the bottles, but they did not prove how well anyone washed. For the next week, the caretaker fitted matching pumps and fixed the leak before we compared the bottles again.

originalGroup.material:
Heritage Name Pronunciation 016

The language club prepared a walking guide to old street names. A map listed a name in writing, but the pupils did not know how local residents pronounced it. A computer voice gave one reading. Two long-term residents used another. The group first thought it had to choose one and call the other wrong.
Their teacher suggested asking where each form was used. The map office said its guide followed the official written form. Residents explained that an older local form was still common in conversation. The pupils recorded both, with the speakers’ permission, and labelled the contexts. They did not claim that two interviews represented every resident. On the final guide, visitors could hear the official guide form and a local spoken form. A note invited further information from the neighbourhood archive.

originalGroup.material:
Canteen Choice Board 016

The canteen displayed three lunch choices on a board. Pupils placed a coloured counter beside their chosen meal before morning lessons. The kitchen used the counts to plan portions. On Tuesday, one ingredient delivery was late. Meal B could not be made. Staff removed its picture at the serving counter, but the morning board still showed it.
